minutes.headline: Green Communities group heard a teen's styrofoam recycling idea and agreed to apply for a small grant this fall.
minutes.summary: A 17-year-old resident presented a styrofoam collection and recycling proposal, and members offered feedback on bin size, location and follow-through. The committee then reviewed the weak list of projects for the competitive Green Communities grant, with mini-split heating and school coordination as the main frustration. Members agreed to apply this fall with what they have, draft an information sheet for departments, and invite the town's Green Communities contact to the September meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed to submit whatever project list it has for the competitive Green Communities grant this fall rather than skip the round.
Members described the current project list as thin: walk-in refrigeration controls at three schools are viable, and the pump station projects have payback periods that are too long.
A member said splitting the mini-split heating project across two grant rounds left no committed grant money, a lost opportunity.
A 17-year-old resident presented a styrofoam collection and recycling idea; the committee offered to help prepare a proposal for the select board and town meeting.
The chair will ask the town's Green Communities contact to the September meeting, and a department checklist of the five eligibility items will be drafted for that contact's review.

why_it_matters: The state's competitive Green Communities grant pays for municipal energy projects, and the committee said the available amount is far from being used by the town's submissions, so the grant the town applies for this year looks small.
A styrofoam recycling program, if it reaches the select board and town meeting, would be a spending or program decision residents may be asked to vote on.
